writeup.headline: Teekay Tankers rates Hold: strong balance sheet and price trend offset by sharply falling revenue.
writeup.thesis: Teekay Tankers scores 60, a Hold, 5 points short of the Buy band. The balance sheet scores a full 100, with net cash and no debt reported in the last 8 quarters, and quality is solid at 75 on a 66.7% gross margin, a 32.5% operating margin and a 12.2% FCF margin, with diluted share count up only 0.2% year on year. The share price trend scores 86: the price is 26.0% above its 200-day average, shares are up 67.7% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and they are 20.2 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Growth is the main drag at 9, with a TTM revenue decline of 22.6% and growth slowed by 6.0 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation could not be scored, and news is mildly positive at 55, helped by record crude tanker rates in early October.
key_risks: Revenue is shrinking, with a TTM revenue decline of 22.6% and growth slowing further.
Tanker rates are cyclical and have already eased from the early October peak.
After a strong run the price is 8.4% below its 52-week high, so a rate pullback could hit the shares.
Directors sold shares near $100 in mid-September, and there has been no insider buying.
Sanctions shifts in the industry could change fleet supply and rates in either direction.
what_would_change: A 5-point gain in the score would reach Buy, most likely from growth improving off its score of 9 if Q3 results on Nov 11 show revenue stabilising.
Firmer news, such as guidance or verified analyst upgrades, could lift the news risk score from 55.
A fall of 16 points would be needed for Sell, for example a sharp break in the price trend combined with weaker margins as rates fall.
